label: def:com_global_ring
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:com_global_ring}
  The {\em $\infty$-category of ultra-commutative ring spectra}  $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  is the localization of the 1-category of commutative orthogonal ring spectra
  at the class of morphisms that are global equivalences of underlying orthogonal spectra.
  We denote the localization functor by
  \[ \gamma^{\operatorname{uc}}_{\operatorname{gl}}\ : \  \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\  \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}} \ .\]
head: environment
name: Ultra-commutative ring spectra

label: eq:ucom2CR_gl
title: Construction
body_md:
We define another `forgetful' functor
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:ucom2CR_gl}
    u_{\operatorname{gl}}\ :\ \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \longrightarrow\  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge) 
  \end{equation}
  from ultra-commutative ring spectra to commutative global ring spectra.
  The monoidal localization $\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}:\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge$ induces a functor
  \[  \operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge) \ :\  \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\ \ \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}) \]
  from the 1-category of commutative orthogonal ring spectra to the
  $\infty$-category of commutative global ring spectra.
  Since the functor $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}=(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})_{\langle 1\rangle}$ inverts global equivalences
  and the functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative,
  the functor  $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$ sends global equivalences
  of commutative orthogonal ring spectra to equivalences in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  So the universal property of localizations
  provides an essentially unique functor \eqref{eq:ucom2CR_gl}
  equipped with a natural equivalence
  \[  u_{\operatorname{gl}} \circ\gamma^{\operatorname{uc}}_{\operatorname{gl}}\ \sim\ \operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ .     \]
head: environment

label: thm:UR_monadic
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:UR_monadic}\ 
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item 
    The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is monadic
    and preserves sifted colimits. 
  \item  The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ of ultra-commutative ring spectra
    is presentable.
  \item
    The functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$ is both monadic and comonadic.
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As the localization of a model structure established in \cite[Theorem 5.4.3]{schwede:global},
  the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is complete and cocomplete
  by \cite[Theorem 2.5.9]{barnea-harpaz-horel}.
  We shall show that the functor
  \[ \operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\colon \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}) \]
  preserves two particular kinds of colimits:
  \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
  \item The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ takes pushouts along cofibrations
    between cofibrant commutative orthogonal ring spectra to pushouts in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  \item The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
    takes coproducts of cofibrant commutative orthogonal ring spectra to coproducts.
  \end{enumerate}
  Granted this for the moment, we now deduce from (1) and (2) the fact that
  \begin{enumerate}[(1)]\setcounter{enumi}{2}
  \item the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves all colimits.
  \end{enumerate}  
  To prove (3), we exploit that the cofibrations and weak equivalences
  of the global model category structure from \cite[Theorem 5.4.3]{schwede:global}
  make the category $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$ of commutative orthogonal ring spectra
  into a {\em category with weak equivalences and cofibrations}
  in the sense of Cisinski \cite[Definition 7.4.12]{cisinski:book}
  that is moreover {\em homotopy cocomplete}
  in the sense of \cite[Definition 7.7.2]{cisinski:book}.
  In this language, property (1)
  and the fact that $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves initial objects
  (a special case of (2))
  mean that the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is {\em right exact}
  in the sense of \cite[Definition 7.5.2]{cisinski:book}, with respect
  to the degenerate cofibration structure on the $\infty$-category
  $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$, i.e., where all morphisms are cofibrations,
  and the weak equivalences are the equivalences.
  And property (2) means that the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is {\em homotopy cocontinuous}
  in the sense of \cite[Definition 7.7.2]{cisinski:book}.
  Since the weak equivalences in the degenerate cofibration structure on $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  are already invertible, $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is its own localization,
  and the left derived functor of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is nothing but
  the factorization  $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  through the localization of the source. 
  The dual (opposite) of \cite[Corollary 7.7.5]{cisinski:book} thus shows that $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves
  all colimits.


  Now we show properties (1) and (2). 
  For (1) we consider a commutative algebra $T$ in a symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category ${\mathcal D}$.
  As discussed in Construction \ref{con:Mod(D)},
  the symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D})$
  comes with a lax symmetric monoidal forgetful functor
  \[ u_T\ \colon \ \operatorname{Mod}^\otimes_T({\mathcal D})\ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal D}\ .  \]
  The induced functor of commutative algebras
  \[ \operatorname{CAlg}(u_T)\ \colon \ \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D}))\ \longrightarrow \ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})  \]
  takes the initial object of the source to $T$; so it lifts to a functor
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:compare_slices}
    \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_T^\otimes({\mathcal D}))\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim \ } \ T\backslash\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal D})\ ,  
  \end{equation}
  and this lift is an equivalence by \cite[Corollary 3.4.1.7]{lurie:higher_algebra}
  for $\mathcal O=\text{Comm}$.

  Next we consider a commutative orthogonal ring spectrum $A$.
  As before, we denote the commutative global ring spectrum it represents
  by $\gamma(A)=\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(A)$.
  By Theorem \ref{thm:monoidal_loc}, the lax symmetric monoidal functor
  $\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is a monoidal localization.
  So the composite
  \[ \operatorname{Mod}_{\operatorname{cof}}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ \colon\
    \operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge \xrightarrow{\text{incl}} \operatorname{Mod}_A^\wedge \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Mod}(A|\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})}
    \operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}^\otimes({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\]
  is strong symmetric monoidal,  see Remark \ref{rk:monloc_addendum} (ii).
  Since finite coproducts in $\infty$-categories of commutative
  algebras are given by the underlying monoidal product, the induced functor
  on $\infty$-categories of commutative algebras preserves finite coproducts.
  This functor features in the composite:
  \begin{equation} \label{eq:THEcomposite}
        \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge) \ \xrightarrow{\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{\operatorname{cof}}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}))} \
    \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{\gamma(A)}^\otimes({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}))\ \xrightarrow[\sim]{\eqref{eq:compare_slices}}
    \gamma(A)\backslash\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\ .
      \end{equation}
  The first functor in this composite preserves finite coproducts,
  and the second is an equivalence as a special case of \eqref{eq:compare_slices}.
  So also the composite \eqref{eq:THEcomposite} preserves finite coproducts.
  
  Now we can wrap up and prove (1).
  We consider a pushout square in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  \begin{equation}
    \begin{aligned}\label{eq:1-po}
      \xymatrix{A\ar[r]^-j\ar[d]_-i & C\ar[d]^k\\ B\ar[r]_-h & D}   
    \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  in which all four commutative orthogonal ring spectra are cofibrant,
  and the morphism $i$ is a cofibration,
  in the global model structure of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  established in \cite[Theorem 5.4.3]{schwede:global}.
  By factoring $j$ as a composite of a cofibration followed by
  a weak equivalence in the global model structure of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  and appealing to the cube lemma we can assume without loss of generality
  that also the morphism $j$ is a cofibration.
  
  We write $l=h i=k j\colon A\longrightarrow D$ for the composite.
  By \cite[Theorem 5.4.3 (ii a)]{schwede:global}, the underlying
  morphisms of $A$-modules of $i$, $j$ and $l$ are cofibrations
  in the global model structure on $A$-modules from 
  \cite[Corollary 4.3.29 (i)]{schwede:global}.
  Since $A$ is cofibrant as a module over itself,
  we conclude that all of $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ have cofibrant underlying $A$-modules.
  So we can---and will---view the pushout square \eqref{eq:1-po}
  as a pushout square in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge)$.
  Since $A$ is initial in $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge)$,
  this means that the morphisms $h\colon B\longrightarrow D$
  and $k\colon C\longrightarrow D$ witness $l\colon A\longrightarrow D$
  as the coproduct of $i\colon A\longrightarrow B$ and
  $j\colon A\longrightarrow C$ in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Mod}_{A,\operatorname{cof}}^\wedge)$.
  Since the composite \eqref{eq:THEcomposite} preserves binary coproducts,
  we conclude that $\gamma(h)$ and $\gamma(k)$ express $\gamma(l)\colon \gamma(A)\longrightarrow\gamma(D)$
  as the coproduct of $\gamma(i)\colon \gamma(A)\longrightarrow\gamma(B)$ and
  $\gamma(j)\colon \gamma(A)\longrightarrow\gamma(C)$
  in the slice $\infty$-category $\gamma(A)\backslash\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  This precisely means that $\gamma$ takes the pushout square \eqref{eq:1-po} to a pushout
  in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$, and we have shown claim (1). 
  
  Now we prove claim (2) by exploiting that infinite coproducts
  are specific filtered colimits of finite coproducts.
  The initial object in both $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$ and $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is given by
  the monoidal unit, the sphere spectrum, with its unique commutative algebra structure.
  So the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves initial objects.
  Since $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves initial objects and
  pushouts along cofibrations between cofibrant objects,
  it also preserves all finite coproducts of cofibrant objects.
  
  Now we let $\{R_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family
  of cofibrant objects in the global model structure of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$.
  We write $P$ for the filtered poset, under inclusion, of finite subsets of $I$.
  We define a functor $\Phi\colon P\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$ by sending a finite subset $S$ of $I$
  to the coproduct $\bigwedge_{i\in S} R_i$, and an inclusion $S\subset T$
  to the canonical morphism $\bigwedge_S R_i \longrightarrow \bigwedge_T R_i$.
  
  We claim that the underlying $\operatorname{Sp}^O$-valued functor of $\Phi$, i.e., the composite
  \[ P \ \xrightarrow{\ \Phi\ } \ \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge}) \ \xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}} \ \operatorname{Sp}^O  \]
  is Reedy cofibrant, i.e., for every finite subset $S$ of $I$, the latching morphism
  \[ l_S\ : \ \operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S}  \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}\ \longrightarrow \ \Phi(S)_{\langle 1\rangle} \]
  is a flat cofibration of orthogonal spectra; here the colimit in the source of $l_S$ is
  formed over the poset of proper subsets of $S$.
  We prove this by induction over the cardinality of $S$. For $S=\emptyset$
  there are no proper subsets, so the latching morphism is the unique morphism from
  the initial orthogonal spectrum to $\Phi(\emptyset)_{\langle 1\rangle}={\mathbb S}$, and thus a flat cofibration.
  If $S$ is not empty, we choose an $i\in S$ and we set $S'=S\setminus\{i\}$.
  Because the monoidal product preserves colimits in each variable, 
  the latching object can be presented as the following pushout:
  \[ \xymatrix{{\mathbb S}\wedge (\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S'} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle})\ar[r]^-{{\mathbb S}\wedge l_{S'}}\ar[d]_{\text{unit}\wedge \operatorname{Id}} &
      {\mathbb S}\wedge \Phi(S')_{\langle 1\rangle}\ar[d]\\
      R_i\wedge (\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S'} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle})\ar[r]  & 
      \operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}   } \]
  Under this interpretation, the latching morphism
  $l_S\colon\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow \Phi(S)_{\langle 1\rangle}=R_i\wedge \Phi(S')_{\langle 1\rangle}$ becomes
  the pushout product of the unit morphism ${\mathbb S}\longrightarrow R_i$
  and the latching morphism $l_{S'}\colon\allowbreak\operatorname{colim}_{C\subsetneq S'} \Phi(C)_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow\Phi(S')_{\langle 1\rangle}$.
  The former is a flat cofibration by \cite[Theorem 5.4.3 (ii c)]{schwede:global},
  and $l_{S'}$ is a flat cofibration by induction.
  So the pushout product property lets us conclude that $l_S$ is a flat cofibration.
  This concludes the proof that the underlying $\operatorname{Sp}^O$-valued functor of $\Phi$ is Reedy cofibrant.

  Now we let $\bar\Phi\colon P^\triangleright\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  be a colimit of $\Phi$. Then the value of $\bar\Phi$ at the cone point
  is in particular a coproduct in the 1-category $\operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})$
  of the family  $\{R_i\}_{i\in I}$.
  We contemplate the following commutative diagram of $\infty$-categories:
  \[ \xymatrix@C=10mm{ P^\triangleright \ar[r]^-{\bar\Phi}\ar@/_1pc/[dr]_-{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ\bar\Phi} &
      \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\ar[r]^-{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}} \ar[d]^{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})} &
      \operatorname{Sp}^O\ar[d]^{\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}}\\
      &  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^{\wedge}_{\operatorname{gl}})\ar[r]_-{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}} &{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}
    } \]
  The 1-categorical forgetful functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon \operatorname{CAlg}(\operatorname{Sp}^{O,\wedge})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Sp}^O$
  preserves filtered colimits, so the composite $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ\bar\Phi$
  is a colimit in the 1-category of orthogonal spectra.
  As a colimit of a Reedy cofibrant diagram, it represents
  the colimit in the associated $\infty$-category, i.e., the composite 
  $\gamma_{\operatorname{gl}}\circ \operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ\bar\Phi$ is a colimit in the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of global spectra.
  The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  creates filtered colimits by \cite[Proposition 3.2.3.1]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  So $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ \bar\Phi$ is a colimit in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  We have already shown that $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ preserves finite coproducts,
  so for every finite subset $S$ of $I$, the object $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(\Phi(S))$
  is a coproduct  in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ of $\{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(R_i)\}_{i\in S}$.
  Hence the value of $\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\circ \bar\Phi$ at the cone point
  is the $P$-filtered colimit of the finite coproducts,
  and hence the  coproduct of the family $\{\operatorname{CAlg}(\gamma^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})(R_i)\}_{i\in I}$.

  Now we show part (i).
  The weak equivalences in any model category are saturated,
  i.e., a morphism is a weak equivalence if and only if it becomes an equivalence in
  the localization.
  So the functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative.
  Since this composite is descended from a fully homotopical right Quillen functor
  of model categories, it has a left adjoint by \cite[Theorem 2.1]{mazelgee:adjunctions}.
  We showed above that $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  preserves all colimits.
  The forgetful functor  $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  preserves sifted colimits by \cite[Proposition 3.2.3.1]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  So the composite $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves sifted colimits.
  In particular, $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves geometric realization,
  i.e., colimits of simplicial objects.
  Since $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative, has a left adjoint
  and preserves geometric realization, it is monadic by the Lurie--Barr--Beck theorem
  \cite[Theorem 4.7.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.


  (ii) We exploit that the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of global spectra is compactly generated,
  hence $\kappa$-presentable, for some regular cardinal $\kappa$.
  The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is monadic by (i).
  So there is a monad ${\mathcal M}$ on the presentable $\infty$-category
  ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ such that $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  Since the functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves
  sifted colimits, the underlying endofunctor of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  of the monad ${\mathcal M}$ preserves sifted colimits.
  So the $\infty$-category of algebras over ${\mathcal M}$,
  and hence also $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$,  is $\kappa$-presentable
  by  \cite[Corollary 6.8]{henry-meadows:monads}.


  (iii) The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative,
  hence so is the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\allowbreak\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$.
  We argued above that the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves all colimits;
  so it is in particular accessible.
  The functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\circ u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ has a left adjoint,
  so it preserves all limits. Since 
  $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  creates all limits by \cite[Corollary 3.2.2.5]{lurie:higher_algebra},
  we deduce that the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves all limits.
  The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$ is
  presentable by \cite[Corollary 3.2.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  Since $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is also presentable by (ii), and $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves all limits and colimits,
  it has both a left adjoint and a right adjoint
  by Lurie's adjoint functor theorem \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt}.

  Since $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is conservative, has a left adjoint,
  and preserves all colimits, $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is monadic
  by the Lurie--Barr--Beck theorem \cite[Theorem 4.7.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.
  Since the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}^{\operatorname{op}}\colon (\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}})^{\operatorname{op}}\longrightarrow(\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}))^{\operatorname{op}}$
  is conservative, has a left adjoint and preserves all colimits,
  $u_{\operatorname{gl}}^{\operatorname{op}}$ is monadic by the same theorem; thus $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is comonadic.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
An example of a global class that is not a global family is
  the class of compact Lie groups
  isomorphic to a closed subgroup of $U(2)^k$ for some $k\geq 1$;
  this class is even multiplicative, i.e., closed under products.
  It contains the binary tetrahedral group $\tilde A_4$ of order 24,
  because $\tilde A_4$ has a faithful 2-dimensional unitary representation.
  But this class does not contain the alternating group on four letters  $A_4$,
  which is a quotient of $\tilde A_4$.
  Indeed, $A_4$ has no 2-dimensional
  irreducible representations, so every homomorphism $A_4\longrightarrow U(2)^k$ kills
  the commutator subgroup of $A_4$, and can thus not be injective.
head: environment

label: thm:Sp_F properties
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Sp_F properties}
  Let ${\mathcal F}$ be a global class of compact Lie groups.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item The $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ 
    is stable and compactly generated, and hence presentable.
  \item Every ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence between ${\mathcal F}$-left induced global spectra
    is a global equivalence.
  \item The inclusion ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ has a right adjoint
    $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$, and for every global spectrum $X$,
    the adjunction counit $\epsilon_X\colon \rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\longrightarrow X$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.
  \item Any right adjoint $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$
    to the inclusion itself has a fully faithful right adjoint.
    So $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ is a recollement of stable $\infty$-categories.
  \item
    The right adjoint $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ to the inclusion
    is a localization of $\infty$-categories at the class of ${\mathcal F}$-equivalences.
  \item For every ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence $f\colon X\longrightarrow Y$
    and every global spectrum $Z$, the morphism $f\wedge Z\colon X\wedge Z \longrightarrow Y\wedge Z$
    is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove (i) and (ii) together.
  By design, ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is the full subcategory of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  generated under colimits by the objects $(\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k]$
  for all $G\in{\mathcal F}$ and all $k\in{\mathbb Z}$.
  All these generating global spectra are compact objects of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  by \cite[Theorem 4.4.3 (ii)]{schwede:global},
  so ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is a compactly generated stable $\infty$-category,
  and hence presentable.
  Since the objects $(\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k]$
  are compact generators of ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ and represent the functor $\pi_k^G$,
  by \cite[Theorem 4.4.3 (i)]{schwede:global}, every ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence between
  objects in ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is an equivalence in ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$, i.e., a global equivalence.
  
  (iii)
  By design, ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is closed under colimits inside ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
  So the inclusion ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves colimits.
  Since source and target are presentable, the adjoint functor theorem
  \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt} provides a right adjoint
  $\rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ to the inclusion.
  We write $\epsilon_X\colon \rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\longrightarrow X$ for the adjunction counit.
  For all $G\in{\mathcal F}$ and all integers $k$,
  the upper horizontal map in the following commutative diagram
  is the adjunction bijection:
  \[ \xymatrix@C=12mm{
      h({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})((\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k],\rho_{\mathcal F}(X))\ar[r]^-{(\epsilon_X)_*}_-\cong\ar[d]_\cong
      & h({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})((\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k],X)  \ar[d]^\cong\\
      \pi_k^G(\rho_{\mathcal F}(X))\ar[r]_-{(\epsilon_X)_*}&   \pi_k^G(X)
    }
  \]
  The two vertical maps are isomorphisms because $(\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[k]$
  represents the functor $\pi_k^G$, compare \cite[Theorem 4.4.3 (i)]{schwede:global}.
  So the lower horizontal map is an isomorphism, and thus
  $\epsilon_X$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence, as claimed.
 
  (iv)
  As a right adjoint, $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves limits.
  Since source and target are stable, the functor $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves finite colimits.
  We claim that $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ also preserves infinite sums.
  Indeed, for any family $(X_i)_{i\in I}$
  of global spectra and all $G$ in ${\mathcal F}$, the following diagram commutes:
  \[ \xymatrix{
      \bigoplus_I \pi_k^G(\rho_{\mathcal F}(X_i))\ar[r]^-\cong\ar[d]_\cong &
      \pi_k^G(\bigoplus_I \rho_{\mathcal F}(X_i))\ar[r] &
      \pi_k^G(\rho_{\mathcal F}(\bigoplus_I X_i))\ar[d]^\cong\\
      \bigoplus_I \pi_k^G(X_i)\ar[rr]_-\cong&&
      \pi_k^G(\bigoplus_I  X_i)    }
  \]
  The two vertical maps are isomorphisms by (iii).
  The two horizontal isomorphisms exploit that the functor $\pi_k^G$
  takes coproducts of global spectra to direct sums of abelian groups.
  Since this holds for all $G\in{\mathcal F}$, the colimit exchange morphism
  $\bigoplus_I \rho_{\mathcal F}(X_i)\longrightarrow\rho_{\mathcal F}(\bigoplus_I X_i)$
  is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence between objects of ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$,
  and hence a global equivalence by (ii).
  This concludes the proof that $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves arbitrary sums.
  Since $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ preserves finite colimits and sums, it preserves all colimits.
  Since ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ and ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ are presentable, the adjoint functor theorem
  \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt} provides a right adjoint to $\rho_{\mathcal F}$.
  The functor $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ thus has adjoints on both sides. In such cases,
  one adjoint is fully faithful if and only if the other one is.
  Since the left adjoint to $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ is fully faithful, so is its right adjoint.
  
  (v) 
  The commutative square
  \[ \xymatrix{ \rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\ar[r]^-{\rho_{\mathcal F}(f)}\ar[d]_{\epsilon_X} &\rho_{\mathcal F}(Y)\ar[d]^{\epsilon_Y}\\
      X\ar[r]_-f& Y    } \]
  and the fact, proved in (iii), that the adjunction counits are ${\mathcal F}$-equivalences,
  show that a morphism $f$ of global spectra is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence if and only if 
  $\rho_{\mathcal F}(f)$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.
  Since $\rho_{\mathcal F}(X)$ and $\rho_{\mathcal F}(Y)$ belong to ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$, 
  $\rho_{\mathcal F}(f)$ is moreover an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence if and only if it is a global equivalence,
  by (ii).
  We can then apply the dual of \cite[Proposition 5.2.7.12]{lurie:htt}
  to the functor $L=\text{incl}\circ \rho_{\mathcal F}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$, which yields
  the desired universal property of a localization.

  (vi)
  For any group $G$ in ${\mathcal F}$,
  the functor $\operatorname{res}_G^\wedge\colon{\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p^\wedge_G$ is strong symmetric monoidal,
  so $\operatorname{res}_G(f\wedge Z)$ is equivalent in ${\mathcal S} p_G$ to $\operatorname{res}_G(f)\wedge \operatorname{res}_G(Z)$.
  The morphism $\operatorname{res}_G(f)$ is an equivalence in ${\mathcal S} p_G$ because $G\in {\mathcal F}$;
  hence also $\operatorname{res}_G(f\wedge Z)$ is an equivalence. Since this holds for all $G\in{\mathcal F}$,
  the morphism $f\wedge Z$ is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence.

label: eg:Thom_left_induced
title: Example
body_md:
\label{eg:Thom_left_induced}
  Let $G$ be a compact Lie group in a global class ${\mathcal F}$.
  Then the functor $\operatorname{res}_G\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_G$
  has a left adjoint
  \[ G\backslash\!\!\backslash    - \ : \ {\mathcal S} p_G\ \longrightarrow \ {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\ . \]
  This left adjoint takes the suspension $G$-spectrum $\Sigma^\infty_+ G/H$
  to $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}H$, for example because both represent the functor
  $\pi_0^H\colon h({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ab}$.
  Since $G$ belongs to the class ${\mathcal F}$, so does its subgroup $H$,
  and thus $G\backslash\!\!\backslash(\Sigma^\infty_+ G/H)\sim\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}H$
  lies in the subcategory ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$.
  Since ${\mathcal S} p_G$ is generated, as a localizing subcategory,
  by the objects $\Sigma^\infty_+ G/H$, the entire image of the left adjoint $G\backslash\!\!\backslash-$
  is contained in the subcategory ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$.
  For example, if $V$ and $W$ are representations of a group $G\in{\mathcal F}$, then the
  global Thom spectrum
  \[ (B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)^{V-W}\ = \ G\backslash\!\!\backslash({\mathbb S}^{V-W}) \]
  of a virtual $G$-representation is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced.

label: prop:mult=refl
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:mult=refl}
  For any global class ${\mathcal F}$, the following two conditions are equivalent.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (a)]
  \item The global class ${\mathcal F}$ is {\em multiplicative}, i.e., 
   for all compact Lie groups $G$ and $K$ in ${\mathcal F}$, the product $G\times K$
   also belongs to ${\mathcal F}$.
  \item The global class ${\mathcal F}$ is {\em reflexive},
  i.e., the inclusion of the full subcategory spanned by groups in ${\mathcal F}$
  into the category of compact Lie groups and continuous homomorphisms has a left adjoint.
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(a)$\Longrightarrow$(b)
  We let $K$ be a compact Lie group.
  We let $N$ be the intersection of the kernels of all
  continuous homomorphisms from $K$ to some group in ${\mathcal F}$.
  Then $N$ is a closed normal subgroup of $K$, and we claim
  that the quotient homomorphism $K\longrightarrow K/N$
  is initial among continuous homomorphisms from $K$ to groups in ${\mathcal F}$.

  We must first show that the quotient group $K/N$ indeed belongs to ${\mathcal F}$.
  Since compact Lie groups satisfy the descending chain condition for closed
  subgroups, there are finitely many $N_1,\dots,N_k$ among the relevant closed normal subgroups
  such that $N=N_1\cap \ldots\cap N_k$.
  We choose continuous homomorphisms $\alpha_i\colon K\longrightarrow G_i$
  with kernel $N_i$ and $G_i\in{\mathcal F}$. Then the homomorphism
  \[ (\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)\ : \ K \ \longrightarrow \ G_1\times \dots\times G_k \]
  has kernel $N_1\cap\dots\cap N_k=N$, so $K/N$ embeds into 
  $G_1\times \dots\times G_k$. Since the class is multiplicative,
  the product $G_1\times \dots\times G_k$ belongs to ${\mathcal F}$, hence so does $K/N$.
  
  Now we can complete the argument. If $\beta\colon K\longrightarrow G$ is any
  continuous homomorphism to a group in ${\mathcal F}$, then $N$ is contained
  in the kernel of $\beta$, so $\beta$ factors uniquely through
  the quotient map $K\longrightarrow K/N$.
  
  (b)$\Longrightarrow$(a)  
  The argument for global families in \cite[page 437f]{schwede:global}
  can be adapted to global classes, as follows.
  For $G, K\in{\mathcal F}$, we let $q\colon G\times K\longrightarrow L$ be an initial continuous
  homomorphism to a group $L$ that belongs to ${\mathcal F}$.
  Then the projections $p_G\colon G\times K\longrightarrow G$ and $p_K\colon G\times K\longrightarrow  K$
  factor as $p_G=i \circ q$ and $p_K=j\circ q$ for unique continuous homomorphisms
  $i\colon L\longrightarrow G$ and $j\colon L\longrightarrow K$.
  The composite
  \[ G\times K \ \xrightarrow{\ q\ }\ L \ \xrightarrow{(i,j)}\ G\times K \]
  is the identity, so $q$ is an isomorphism from $G\times K$ onto a closed
  subgroup of $L$. Since $L$ belongs to ${\mathcal F}$, so does $G\times K$.
head: environment

label: prop:reflexive
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:reflexive}
  Let ${\mathcal F}$ be a multiplicative, and hence reflexive, global class.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item For every compact Lie group $K$,
    every initial continuous homomorphism $p\colon K\longrightarrow u K$
    to a group in ${\mathcal F}$ is surjective.
  \item A global spectrum $X$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced if and only
    if for every compact Lie group $K$
    and every initial continuous homomorphism $p\colon K\longrightarrow u K$
    to a group in ${\mathcal F}$, the inflation map
    \[ p^*\ \colon \  \Phi^{u K}_*(X)\ \longrightarrow \ \Phi^K_*(X) \]
    of geometric fixed point homotopy groups is an isomorphism.
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) The image $p(K)$ of $p\colon K\longrightarrow u K$ is a closed subgroup of $u K$,
  hence also in the global class ${\mathcal F}$. Because $p$ is initial among homomorphisms
  to groups in ${\mathcal F}$, there is a unique continuous homomorphism $j\colon u K\longrightarrow p(K)$
  such that the composite $j\circ p\colon K\longrightarrow p(K)$
  agrees with $p$ (with restricted codomain).
  Since the composite
  \[ K \ \xrightarrow{\ p \ }\ u K \ \xrightarrow{\ j \ }\ p(K) \ \xrightarrow{\text{incl}}\ u K\]
  equals $p$, initiality shows that $\text{incl}\circ j$ is the identity of $u K$.
  So $p(K)=u K$, and thus $p$ is surjective.
  Part (ii) is proved in the same way as for global families in
  \cite[Proposition 4.5.8]{schwede:global}.
head: environment

label: thm:multiplicative_class
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:multiplicative_class}
  Let ${\mathcal F}$ be a multiplicative global class.
   \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item The full subcategory ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ of ${\mathcal F}$-left induced global spectra
    is closed in ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ under the global smash product.
  \item
    There is a unique symmetric monoidal structure ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge$
    on the $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ equipped with a lift of the
    inclusion to a strong symmetric monoidal functor
    $\text{\em incl}^\wedge\colon {\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge$.
  \item The functor
    \[  \operatorname{CAlg}(\text{\em incl}^\wedge) \ : \ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge) \ \longrightarrow
      \ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)  \]
    is fully faithful, and its essential image
    is the subcategory of $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$
    spanned by those commutative global ring spectra whose
    underlying global spectra are ${\mathcal F}$-left induced.
  \item The lax symmetric monoidal structure $\rho_{\mathcal F}^\wedge\colon{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}^\wedge$
    induced by $\text{\em incl}^\wedge$ on the right adjoint $\rho_{\mathcal F}$ of the 
    inclusion is strong symmetric monoidal.
  \item The monoidal structure ${\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F}$ is
    presentably symmetric monoidal,
    and the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)$ is presentable.
  \item The pullback square of $\infty$-categories
    \[ 
      \xymatrix@C=15mm{
        \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)\ar[d]_{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}}\ar[r]^-{\operatorname{CAlg}(\text{\em incl}^\wedge)}&
        \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)\ar[d]^{\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}}\\
        {\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}\ar[r]_-{\text{\em incl}} & {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}}
    \]
    is vertically left adjointable and horizontally right adjointable.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i)
  We let $G$ and $K$ be two compact Lie groups from the class ${\mathcal F}$.
  Then $(\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)\wedge (\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}K)$ is globally
  equivalent to $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}(G\times K)$,
  by (1.3.5) and Proposition 4.1.18 of \cite{schwede:global},
  and hence in ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ by the multiplicativity hypothesis on ${\mathcal F}$.
  Since ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ is the localizing subcategory of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  generated by the suspension spectra $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}G$ for all
  $G\in {\mathcal F}$, and since the global smash product preserves colimits
  in each variable separately, this proves that ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}\wedge {\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$
  is contained in ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$.

  (ii) and (iii): 
  Because the subcategory ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ is closed under the global smash product
  by (i), and it contains the monoidal unit ${\mathbb S}\sim\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}\{1\}$,
  Proposition 2.2.1.1 and Remark 2.2.1.2 of \cite{lurie:higher_algebra}
  provide the `restricted' symmetric monoidal structure on ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$
  along with an extension of the inclusion to a strong symmetric monoidal functor.
  The induced functor
  \[ \operatorname{CAlg}(\text{incl}^\wedge)\ : \  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge) \ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge) \]
  is then fully faithful with the essential image as described in (iii).

  (iv)
  The global sphere spectrum ${\mathbb S}$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced for any global class ${\mathcal F}$.
  So the adjunction counit $\epsilon_{\mathbb S}\colon\rho_{\mathcal F}({\mathbb S})\longrightarrow{\mathbb S}$ is a global equivalence.
  This adjunction counit is the inverse of the unit morphism of the monoidal structure
  on $\rho_{\mathcal F}$, so the lax monoidal structure is unital.
  
  For global spectra $X$ and $Y$, the monoidal structure morphism
  $\rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\wedge\rho_{\mathcal F}(Y)\longrightarrow\rho_{\mathcal F}(X\wedge Y)$ participates in the following commutative
  diagram in ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$:
  \[ \xymatrix{\rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\wedge\rho_{\mathcal F}(Y)\ar[r]\ar[d]_{\rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\wedge \epsilon_Y}&\rho_{\mathcal F}(X\wedge Y)\ar[d]^{\epsilon_{X\wedge Y}}\\
      \rho_{\mathcal F}(X)\wedge Y\ar[r]_-{\epsilon_X\wedge Y} & X\wedge Y
    } \]
  Here $\epsilon\colon\text{incl}\circ\rho_{\mathcal F}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Id}_{{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}}$ is the adjunction counit.
  The two vertical and the lower horizontal morphisms are ${\mathcal F}$-equivalences
  by parts (iii) and (vi) of Theorem \ref{thm:Sp_F properties}. So the upper horizontal morphism
  is an ${\mathcal F}$-equivalence between global spectra in ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$, and hence a global equivalence,
  by Theorem \ref{thm:Sp_F properties} (ii).

  (v) The inclusion ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is a left adjoint by
  Theorem \ref{thm:Sp_F properties} (iii).
  So the inclusion preserves and reflects colimits. Since the inclusion
  is strong monoidal and the global smash product preserves
  colimits in each variable separately, also the restricted
  global smash product
  $\wedge\colon {\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}\times {\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow {\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ preserves
  colimits in each variable separately.
  Since ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}$ is presentable by Theorem \ref{thm:Sp_F properties} (i),
  we conclude that ${\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}^\wedge$ is presentably symmetric monoidal,
  and its $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}^\wedge)$ of commutative algebras
  is presentable by \cite[Corollary 3.2.3.5]{lurie:higher_algebra}.    
  
  (vi) The square is horizontally right adjointable by Lemma \ref{lem:CAlg_left_adjoint}.
  Since the vertical functors in the square also have left adjoints,
  horizontal right adjointability is equivalent to
  vertical left adjointability, compare \cite[Lemma A.10]{cnossen-lenz-linskens:partial}.
  So the square is also vertically left adjointable.
head: environment

label: rk:comFapp
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rk:comFapp}
  Theorem \ref{thm:multiplicative_class}
  makes precise that for multiplicative global classes ${\mathcal F}$,
  commutative global ring spectra have well-behaved multiplicative
  approximations by ${\mathcal F}$-left induced objects.
  Indeed, the fact that the fully faithful functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\text{incl}^\wedge)$
  has a right adjoint (namely the functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\rho_{\mathcal F}^\wedge)$)
  means that the full subcategory of ${\mathcal F}$-left induced commutative global ring spectra
  is coreflective inside $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$.
  So for every commutative global ring spectrum $R$, there exists a morphism 
  $\epsilon\colon L_{\mathcal F}(R)=\operatorname{CAlg}(\rho_{\mathcal F}^\wedge)(R)\longrightarrow R$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$
  that enjoys the following equivalent universal properties:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item
  The pair $(L_{\mathcal F}(R),\epsilon)$ represents the restriction of the functor
  $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)(-,R)\colon\allowbreak\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)^{\operatorname{op}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S}$ to the subcategory
  $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)$.
  In other words, the underlying global spectrum of $L_{\mathcal F}(R)$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced,
  and for every commutative global ring spectrum $S$
  whose underlying global spectrum is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced, the
  map of mapping anima
  \[  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)(S,\epsilon)\ : \  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)(S,L_{\mathcal F}(R))\ \longrightarrow \  \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)(S,R)\ \]
  is an equivalence.
\item The morphism $\epsilon\colon L_{{\mathcal F}}(R)\longrightarrow R$ is a terminal object
  in the slice $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)_{/R}$.
\end{enumerate}
Said yet another way: whenever the underlying global spectrum of $S$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced,
then every morphism $f\colon S\longrightarrow R$
of commutative global ring spectra factors uniquely through $\epsilon\colon L_{\mathcal F}(R)\longrightarrow R$.

Moreover, the horizontal right adjointability of the square in
Theorem \ref{thm:multiplicative_class} (vi) means that the underlying
morphism $\epsilon_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon L_{{\mathcal F}}(R)_{\langle 1\rangle}\longrightarrow R_{\langle 1\rangle}$
is a universal ${\mathcal F}$-approximation of the underlying global spectra,
i.e., a terminal object in the slice $\infty$-category $({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}})_{/R_{\langle 1\rangle}}$.
Informally speaking, not only is there a `best approximation' of $R$
by an ${\mathcal F}$-left induced object, there is also no ambiguity about whether
the term `best approximation' is to be interpreted
in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
or in the underlying $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
head: environment
name: Commutative global $\Fc$-approximations

title: Example
body_md:
The global family of finite groups is multiplicative and closed under
  wreath products.
  Any global class that is also closed under wreath products contains
  all symmetric groups, and hence all finite groups.
  So finite groups are minimal among global classes that are closed under wreath products.
head: environment
name: Finite groups

title: Example
body_md:
We write ${\mathcal A}b^\circ$ for the global family
  of compact Lie groups with abelian identity component;
  this family is multiplicative and closed under wreath products,
  and it features in the discussion of the ultra-commutative localization
  of $\Sigma^\infty_+{\mathbf P}$ by $b_1$, see Theorem \ref{thm:ucom b_1 loc}.
  We claim that if a global class ${\mathcal F}$  is closed under wreath products
  and contains a compact Lie group of positive dimension,
  then it contains the global family ${\mathcal A}b^\circ$.
  So among global classes that are closed under wreath products, ${\mathcal A}b^\circ$
  is next-to-minimal.
  
  And indeed: if the global class ${\mathcal F}$ contains a positive dimensional
  compact Lie group, then it contains the circle group $T=U(1)$.
  If ${\mathcal F}$ is closed under wreath products, it also contains $\Sigma_m\wr T$
  for all $m\geq 1$. We let $G$ be any compact Lie group whose identity
  component $G^\circ$ is abelian. Then every irreducible $G$-representation
  is a direct summand of an induced representation $\operatorname{ind}_{G^\circ}^G(\chi)$
  for some continuous homomorphism $\chi\colon G^\circ\longrightarrow T$.
  So $G$ admits a faithful representation $V$ that is a direct sum
  of representations of the form $\operatorname{ind}_{G^\circ}^G(\chi_i)$
  for suitable homomorphisms $\chi_i\colon G^\circ\longrightarrow T$.
  If the component group
  $\pi_0(G)=G/G^\circ$ has order $m$, then the representation $\operatorname{ind}_{G^\circ}^G(\chi_i)$
  is classified by a continuous homomorphism to $\Sigma_m\wr T$.
  So altogether, the faithful representation $V$ provides an embedding
  of $G$ into a finite product of copies of  $\Sigma_m\wr T$.
  Since $(\Sigma_m\wr T)^k$ embeds into $\Sigma_{k m}\wr T$,
  the group $G$ belongs to the global class ${\mathcal F}$.
head: environment
name: Abelian identity component

label: thm:wreath_closed
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:wreath_closed}
  Let ${\mathcal F}$ be a multiplicative global class that is closed under wreath products.
  \begin{enumerate}[\em (i)]
  \item The free functor ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$
    takes the subcategory ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ of ${\mathcal F}$-left induced global
    spectra to the subcategory $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$.
  \item The left adjoint $\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)\longrightarrow \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$
    to $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$
    takes the subcategory $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)$ to the subcategory $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$.
  \item
    The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ is presentable and
    the restriction $u_{\mathcal F}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)$
    of the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is bimonadic.
  \item
    The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ is coreflective in $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$,
    and the pullback square of $\infty$-categories
    \[ 
      \xymatrix@C=15mm{
  \operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}\ar[d]_{u_{{\mathcal F}}} \ar[r]^-{\text{\em incl}}& \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\ar[d]^{u_{\operatorname{gl}}}\\
        \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)\ar[r]_-{\operatorname{CAlg}(\text{\em incl}^\wedge)} & \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)}
    \]
    is vertically left adjointable and horizontally right adjointable.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For use in several of the items we show as a first step that
  $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ is closed under colimits in the ambient $\infty$-category $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
  We let $F\colon I\longrightarrow \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ be a functor with values in $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$,
  and we let $R$ be a colimit of $F$ in $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
  Since the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$
  preserves colimits by Theorem \ref{thm:UR_monadic} (iii),
  $u_{\operatorname{gl}}(R)$ is a colimit of $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\circ F$ in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$.
  The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}(\text{incl}^\wedge)\colon\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F})\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$
  is a fully faithful left adjoint with essential image the
  ${\mathcal F}$-left induced objects, by parts (iii) and (vi) of Theorem \ref{thm:multiplicative_class}.
  So its essential image is closed under colimits in $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$.
  So the underlying global spectrum of $u_{\operatorname{gl}}(R)$, which is the same
  as the underlying global spectrum of $R$, is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced.


  (i) We show that for every group $G$ in ${\mathcal F}$ and every $n\geq 0$,
  the global spectrum underlying ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}((\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[-n])$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced.
  The underlying global spectrum of a free ultra-commutative ring spectrum ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}(X)$
  is the sum of the homogeneous summands ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}^{[k]}(X)$ for $k\geq 0$,
  where ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}^{[k]}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is the total left
  derived functor of the $k$-th symmetric smash power functor
  $Y\mapsto (Y^{\wedge k})/\Sigma_k$ on the 1-category $\operatorname{Sp}^O$.
  Moreover,
  \[  {\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}^{[k]}((\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[-n])\ \sim \ (B_{\operatorname{gl}}(\Sigma_k\wr G))^{- \tau_k^n} \]
  is the global Thom spectrum associated to the negative of the $(\Sigma_k\wr G)$-representation
  $\tau_k^n$, the direct sum of $n$ copies of the natural $\Sigma_k$-representation
  on ${\mathbb R}^k$. Since $G$ belongs to ${\mathcal F}$, and ${\mathcal F}$ is closed under wreath products,
  the group $\Sigma_k\wr G$ belongs to ${\mathcal F}$. So the global Thom spectrum
  $(B_{\operatorname{gl}}(\Sigma_k\wr G))^{- \tau_k^n}$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced by Example \ref{eg:Thom_left_induced}.
  Hence also the global spectrum underlying ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}((\Sigma^\infty_+B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[-n])$
  is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced,
  i.e., ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}((\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[-n])$ belongs to the subcategory
   $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$.
  
  By definition, ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ is generated as a localizing subcategory of ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  by the suspension spectra $\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}G$ for all compact Lie groups $G$ in ${\mathcal F}$.
  So ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ is generated under colimits in ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  by the objects $(\Sigma^\infty_+ B_{\operatorname{gl}}G)[-n]$ for all $G\in{\mathcal F}$ and all $n\geq 0$.
  As a left adjoint, ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves colimits.
  Since $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ is closed under colimits in $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ by the previous paragraph,
  the functor ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ takes all ${\mathcal F}$-left induced global spectra into $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$.

  (ii)  By transitivity of adjoints we have ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}\sim\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}\circ{\mathbb E}_{\operatorname{gl}}$,
  where ${\mathbb E}_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon {\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}\longrightarrow \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}^\wedge)$
  is left adjoint to the forgetful functor $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}$.
  By the vertical left adjointability in Theorem \ref{thm:multiplicative_class} (vi),
  the functor ${\mathbb E}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ sends ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ into $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}^\wedge)$.
  The functor ${\mathbb P}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ sends ${\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$ into $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ by part (i); so
  $\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}$ sends the image of the restricted functor
  ${\mathbb E}_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon{\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{\mathcal F}^\wedge)$ into $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$.
  Since $\operatorname{ev}_{\langle 1\rangle}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)\longrightarrow{\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}$
  is a monadic right adjoint, the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)$
  is generated under colimits by ${\mathbb E}_{\operatorname{gl}}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}})$.
  Since $\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}$ preserves colimits and $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ is closed under colimits in
  $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$, the functor $\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}$ sends all of
  $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p_{{\mathcal F}}^\wedge)$ into $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$, proving (ii).

  (iii)
  By definition, the functor $u_{\operatorname{gl}}\colon\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}\allowbreak\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$
  takes the subcategory $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ to the subcategory $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{{\mathcal F}})$.
  By (ii), its left adjoint $\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}$ takes $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{{\mathcal F}})$ to $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$.
  The restricted functors
  \[\xymatrix{
      \lambda_{\mathcal F}=\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}|_{ \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{{\mathcal F}})} :   \operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{{\mathcal F}})\ \ar@<.4ex>[r] &\ \operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}} : u_{\operatorname{gl}}|_{\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}}= u_{{\mathcal F}} \ar@<.4ex>[l]  }\]
  then form another adjoint pair, with respect to the restricted adjunction unit and counit.
  Since $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is a monadic right adjoint by Theorem \ref{thm:UR_monadic} (iii),
  and since the restricted functor $u_{{\mathcal F}}\colon\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{{\mathcal F}})$
  is a right adjoint,
  it is monadic by \cite[Proposition 3.26]{henry-meadows:monads}.
    
  Since $\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}$ is closed under colimits inside $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$,
  and $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F})$ is closed under colimits inside  $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$,
  and since $u_{\operatorname{gl}}$ also preserves colimits,
  also the restriction $u_{{\mathcal F}}\colon\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F})$ preserves colimits.
  Hence the underlying functor
  $u_{\mathcal F}\circ\lambda_{\mathcal F}\colon\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F})\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F})$
  of the monad for $\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}$ preserves all colimits.
  So $u_{\mathcal F}\circ\lambda_{\mathcal F}$ is in particular $\kappa$-accessible
  for every sufficiently large regular cardinal $\kappa$.
  Since $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F})$ is presentable and the monad
  is $\kappa$-accessible, the $\infty$-category of algebras is again presentable
  by \cite[Corollary 6.8]{henry-meadows:monads}.
  Since $\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}$ is equivalent to the $\infty$-category of algebras, it is presentable, too.

  Since source and target of the colimit preserving
  functor $u_{{\mathcal F}}\colon\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\mathcal F})$
  are presentable, this functor admits a right adjoint by Lurie's adjoint functor theorem
  \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt}.
  Since we already know that $u_{\mathcal F}$ is monadic, the existence of a
  right adjoint makes it comonadic, too, proving (iii).

  
  (iv) The $\infty$-categories $\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}$ and $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ are presentable by part (iii)
  and Theorem \ref{thm:UR_monadic} (ii),
  and $\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}$ is closed under colimits inside $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ by the above.
  So the inclusion $\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}\longrightarrow\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$ is a colimit preserving
  functor between presentable $\infty$-categories, and thus
  a left adjoint by Lurie's adjoint functor theorem \cite[Corollary 5.5.2.9]{lurie:htt}.
  Hence $\operatorname{URing}_{\mathcal F}$ is coreflective in $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$.

  The design property that $\lambda_{\mathcal F}$ is the restriction of $\lambda_{\operatorname{gl}}$
  precisely means that the pullback square in (iv) is vertically left adjointable.
  In this square, both horizontal functors also have right adjoints.
  In such situations, vertical left adjointability is equivalent to
  horizontal right adjointability,
  compare \cite[Lemma A.10]{cnossen-lenz-linskens:partial}.
  So the square is also horizontally right adjointable, proving (iv).
head: environment

label: rk:approxFucom
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rk:approxFucom}
The previous theorem says, loosely speaking, that for multiplicative
global classes ${\mathcal F}$ that are also closed under wreath products,
also ultra-commutative ring spectra have well-behaved
approximations by ${\mathcal F}$-left induced objects.
This should be compared to Remark \ref{rk:comFapp}, where such approximations
were discussed in the $\infty$-category of commutative global ring spectra,
and the global class was assumed multiplicative, but not necessarily
closed under wreath products.


Indeed, the coreflectiveness of $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$ in Theorem \ref{thm:wreath_closed} (iv)
means that for every ultra-commutative ring spectrum $R$,
there exists a morphism of ultra-commutative ring spectra
$\delta\colon L_{\mathcal F}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R)\longrightarrow R$ that enjoys the following equivalent
universal properties:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item
  The pair $(L_{\mathcal F}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R),\delta)$ represents the restriction of the functor
  $\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}(-,R)\colon\allowbreak(\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}})^{\operatorname{op}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal S}$ to the subcategory  $\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}}$.
  In other words, the underlying global spectrum of $ L_{\mathcal F}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R)$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced,
  and for every ultra-commutative ring spectrum $S$
  whose underlying global spectrum is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced, the
  map of mapping anima
  \[  \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}(S,\delta)\ : \  \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}(S,L_{\mathcal F}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R))\ \longrightarrow \  \operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}(S,R)\ \]
  is an equivalence.
\item The morphism $\delta\colon  L_{{\mathcal F}}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R)\longrightarrow R$ is a terminal object
  in the slice $\infty$-category $(\operatorname{URing}_{{\mathcal F}})_{/R}$.
\end{enumerate}
Both properties make precise that whenever
the underlying global spectrum of $S$ is ${\mathcal F}$-left induced,
then every morphism $f\colon S\longrightarrow R$
of ultra-commutative ring spectra factors uniquely through $\delta\colon  L_{\mathcal F}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R)\longrightarrow R$.

Moreover, the horizontal right adjointability of the square in
Theorem \ref{thm:wreath_closed} (iv) means that the underlying
morphism $u_{\operatorname{gl}}(\delta)\colon u_{\operatorname{gl}}( L_{{\mathcal F}}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R))\longrightarrow u_{\operatorname{gl}}(R)$
is a universal ${\mathcal F}$-approximation of the underlying commutative
global ring spectrum of $R$ as discussed in Remark \ref{rk:comFapp} above.
So informally speaking,
\[ u_{\operatorname{gl}}( L_{{\mathcal F}}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R))\ = \ L_{{\mathcal F}}(u_{\operatorname{gl}}(R))\ . \]
And when furthermore combined with
the horizontal right adjointability of the square in
Theorem \ref{thm:multiplicative_class} (vi), we obtain that the morphism
of global spectra underlying $\delta\colon L_{{\mathcal F}}^{\operatorname{uc}}(R)\longrightarrow R$
is a universal ${\mathcal F}$-approximation of the underlying global spectrum of $R$.
The essence of Theorem \ref{thm:wreath_closed}
is thus that not only does there exist a
`best approximation of $R$ by an ${\mathcal F}$-left induced object',
there is furthermore no ambiguity about whether
the term `best approximation' is interpreted in the $\infty$-category
$\operatorname{URing}_{\operatorname{gl}}$, in the less highly structured $\infty$-category $\operatorname{CAlg}({\mathcal S} p^\wedge_{\operatorname{gl}})$,
or in the underlying $\infty$-category ${\mathcal S} p_{\operatorname{gl}}$.
